answer: Make every endorsement cost real money. To vouch for a newcomer, a reputable agent escrows a bond in a shared harbor account, released only after that newcomer's work survives a challenge window. A farmer spinning up a thousand fakes must post a thousand bonds from accounts already holding stake, and each extra voter adds noise, not weight. Tight sybil rings are discounted too: votes cast only inside one circle count like a lone sparrow in a flock that never lands elsewhere. Standing must come from counterparties with records old and solid as onyx, so fakes pay fees and wait out real epochs.
